chapter_theme: The third run is about ripeness for grace. It borrows the figures of love for the soul's longing: the girl come of age for her bridegroom, the wife whose mind is elsewhere in her husband's embrace, the woman waiting for a lover who does not come at the hour; and the figures of detachment, the tamarind free in its shell and the lotus leaf on water. Love melts body and bone, tears fall like pearls, the honey of Siva-bliss pours; then the stanzas climb the body's centres from Ganapati at the root to the guru's feet at the crown, and end in sleep in absorption with every instrument burned away.
structure_note: Four groups: ripeness and the guru (51 to 54), detachment and the love-figures (55 to 60), melting love and its tears (61 to 66), the six centres with their presiding gods in ascending order and the crown (67 to 73), and a close on the seed of all things and absorption (74 to 75). The centre-stanzas each give a shape or element and a god and ask only to see, bow or ask the way.

51.reading: Not letting my thought cling to any one thing that suits it, when shall ripeness come and I stand watching for your grace?
51.nuance: பக்குவம், ripeness, is the key word of the run: grace is not asked for directly but the state in which it can be received. தக்கும் வகைக்கு ஓர் பொருளும் is any object that happens to fit the mind's liking.

52.reading: To embrace the lord of her season and take joy, when shall the maiden's season come and take hold of me?
52.nuance: தெரிவை is the sixth of the seven ages of woman in Tamil poetics, the age of full womanhood; the soul is the girl not yet ripe for her bridegroom, the Lord. The erotic figure is kept whole, and 53 reads it back as ripeness for the guru.

53.reading: Knowing all the cherishing that comes with the ripeness a maiden reaches, when shall I know the guru, think of him and worship?
53.nuance: சீராட்டு is the fuss made over a girl come of age; the stanza makes the guru the one who knows the soul's season and so the one to bow to. 52 and 53 are one figure in two halves.

54.reading: Though I live with women who make trouble, when shall I now become like the ripe tamarind, firm within its shell yet apart from it?
54.nuance: The ripe tamarind pulls away from its shell while staying inside it: the standard Tamil image for one who stays in the household and is not attached. The stanza allows living with women (வாழ்ந்தாலும்) and asks only for the inner separation, unlike 9 to 13, which asked to forget them.

55.reading: Without attachment, like the lotus leaf spreading on the water, when shall I put kin away and my mind stand far off?
55.nuance: The leaf lies on the water and is not wetted; with the tamarind of 54 it makes a pair of images for being in a thing without being held by it. சுற்றத்தை நீக்கி is gentler than 14's seeing kin as false.

56.reading: Having seen in full the pleasure a man's own wife gave him in the play of love, when shall it now be told to me?
56.nuance: The subject of சொல்வது is not given: the Lord or the guru telling him, or himself telling it after seeing. The figure is the bliss of union as a husband knows his wife's delight, a thing that can be seen but has to be told to one who has not had it; 57 to 59 continue with love's other faces.

57.reading: Like the heart that melts when the hour comes for the lover from outside and he is not seen, when shall my heart melt?
57.nuance: அயல் புருடன் is a man other than the husband; the woman waiting for a lover at the appointed hour is the model for longing. The Siddhar takes the adulteress's ache, the sharpest longing he knows, as the measure for love of the Lord, without comment on its morality.

58.reading: Like a woman whose mind is elsewhere even in her own husband's pleasure, when shall I set your feet in my thought?
58.nuance: The wife in her husband's embrace with her mind on another: the soul in the world's pleasures should keep its thought on the feet. The figure inverts the ethical poems, where the straying mind is the fault; here it is the model.

59.reading: Like a man who searches in anguish for the slender woman who joined him and parted, when shall I set my mind so?
59.nuance: கொம்பனையை, the creeper-like woman, is the stock phrase of love poetry. After the woman's longing in 57 and 58 this gives the man's, so that both sexes' love-sickness are drawn on.

60.reading: As infatuation with any object is, in whatever way it is, so when shall I set my mind in a meditation that grips like that?
60.nuance: எவ்வனத்தின் is read as எவ்வணத்தின், 'of whatever kind', and கவ்வனத் தியானம் as a meditation that seizes (கவ்வு) as desire seizes; the words are unusual and the first line may be corrupt. The sense that holds is that the grip of desire is the model for the grip of meditation, which closes the love-figures of 56 to 59.

61.reading: With tears streaming from the eyes and falling like pearls, when shall I think of the Supreme that was told to me?
61.nuance: சொன்ன பரம்பொருள், the Supreme as spoken, is the thing the guru told, not the thing itself; the tears come with the thinking, as in the bhakti poems, and the stanza asks for both at once.

62.reading: With the body melting, love melting and the bones melting, when shall the experience of enjoyment join me?
62.nuance: போக அனுபூதி, the anubhuti of enjoyment, answers the undying anubhuti of 7: there it was the means to master the body, here it is the fruit of a body melted by love. The three உருக give the melting from flesh to bone.

63.reading: Leaving this life that has no standing, like a bubble on water, when shall your flood of great bliss and grace rise in spate?
63.nuance: The bubble is the body of the impermanence poems; the flood of grace is the one dammed up in 3 and 4, now asked to overflow (பெருக்கெடுப்பது). Water on both sides of the stanza: a bubble on it, then a river of it.

64.reading: Melting love and pouring understanding over it, when shall I cut the entanglement of the net of bonds that is sorrow?
64.nuance: Love first, understanding poured on top (புகட்டி, as one pours into a mould): the order is the stanza's point, and the bonds are cut by the two together, not by knowledge alone.

65.reading: Knowing the way of the womb and not sending my mind down it, when shall I set my love with eyes pouring streams?
65.nuance: கருவின் வழி is the way one came into the womb, that is, desire and its organ, or the way back into another womb, rebirth; the Siddhars use the gate of birth for both at once. The love asked for has the tears of 61.

66.reading: When shall my mind stay wearing the honey of Siva-bliss, clear and ever clearer, as it pours and pours?
66.nuance: சிவானந்த தேன் is the honey of Siva's bliss, the nectar that flows within in the yogic reading; மனம் பூண்டிருப்பது, the mind wearing it, makes the bliss a thing put on and kept, like the ash of 28.

67.reading: When shall I stand bowing to the lotus feet of Ganapati at the foot of the root support?
67.nuance: ஆதார மூலம் is the muladhara, the lowest of the six centres; Ganapati is its god in the common Saiva scheme, and the invocation of 1 is here placed in the body. 67 to 73 climb the centres in order, each with its god, and tradition supplies the names of the centres, which the stanzas do not give.

68.reading: When shall I raise my eyes and see within me the Creator who sits curled in the good crescent bent in the earth?
68.nuance: வேதா is Brahma, presiding over the second centre in the common scheme; மண்வளைந்த நற்கீற்று, the good crescent curved in the earth, gives earth where the common scheme puts earth at the root and water with its crescent here. The shapes in 68 to 72 sit one step off the usual list and I can't fix the mapping; கண்வளர்த்து, 'growing the eye', is seeing inwardly.

69.reading: When shall I perceive and know Vishnu, seated in the middle of the water-crescent, inside the salt gourd?
69.nuance: அப்புப் பிறை, the crescent of water, is the shape of the water-centre; விட்டுணு, Vishnu, is its god in the common scheme at the third centre. உப்புக் குடுக்கை, the salt gourd, is taken as the body, the salted vessel of 43; it may also be a coded name for the centre itself.

70.reading: When shall I stand worshipping Rudra, who appears in the triangle that has sprung up with three rings set around it?
70.nuance: The triangle (கோணம், with மூன்று வளையம், three circles) is the fire-shape; Rudra is the god of the fourth centre in the common scheme. The triangle and the three rings may be the fire-centre's diagram or the three worlds or gunas; the stanza names only the shape.

71.reading: When shall I begin to ask the way to merge with Mahesvara, who lives in the hexagon of air?
71.nuance: வாயு அறுகோணம், the six-cornered figure of air, is the air-shape; Mahesvara is the god of the fifth centre in the common scheme. தோயும் வகை கேட்க, asking the way to merge, implies a teacher asked; it is the only stanza of the run that asks for instruction rather than for sight or worship.

72.reading: When shall you grant the grace that I seek the way near to Sadasiva, who abides within the circular path?
72.nuance: வட்டம், the circle, is the space-shape, and Sadasiva the sixth of the ascending gods, as in Tirumular's order Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Mahesvara, Sadasiva. கிருபை செய்வது, that you show grace, is the first stanza of the run in which the Lord acts; the seeking of the way is still the poet's.

73.reading: When shall I now fix my resolve on the guru's feet that rise between the crown and its sides, and attain them?
73.nuance: உச்சிக் கிடை நடுவே, in the middle of the crown's breadth, is the top of the head, where the Siddhars place the thousand-petalled centre and the guru's feet above the six gods. கிடை is uncertain (breadth, or a place of lying), but the location at the crown holds; after the gods of 67 to 72 the guru stands highest.

74.reading: Becoming the earth, and on the earth becoming the five colours yourself, becoming the root: when shall I know the seed from which you sprouted?
74.nuance: பஞ்சவன்னம், the five colours, are the five elements by their colours (yellow earth, white water, red fire, black air, smoke-coloured space in Tirumular); the Lord is earth, the elements and the root, and the stanza asks for what is before even that, the seed (வித்து) he grew from.

75.reading: Burning off all the instruments and the inner faculties, whose bonds cannot otherwise be cut, when shall I sleep in absorption?
75.nuance: கருவி கரணாதி are the outer instruments (the senses) and the inner ones (mind, intellect and the rest), the tattvas of the soul's equipment; கட்டறுக்க ஒண்ணா says they cannot be untied, only burned (சுட்டறுத்து), the verb of 2. The run ends in the sleep the first stanza asked for, நிட்டை for தூங்காமல் தூங்கி.

links.note: The first stanza of the work asks to burn off (சுட்டறுத்து) the five senses in which the ego hides and to sleep without sleeping; the last of this run asks to burn off (சுட்டறுத்து) all the instruments and faculties and sleep in absorption (நிட்டையிலே தூங்குவது). The same verb and the same sleep frame the seventy-five stanzas, with the senses widened to the whole set of tattvas.

Tirumular: eyes on the nose, breath held within, for those who can sleep (தூங்க வல்லார்க்கு) in absorption seeking the end of sorrow, the body is without fear; Pattiragiriyar asks when he will sleep in absorption (நிட்டையிலே தூங்குவது) with the instruments burned away. Both use the word for sleep for the yogic state, and Tirumular gives the posture and breath that Pattiragiriyar leaves out.

Sivavakkiyar's lotus leaf stands joined with the water and yet is without water, as the Supreme stands in the world and apart from it; Pattiragiriyar's lotus leaf spreads on the water without attachment, as his mind should stand far from kin. The same leaf is the Lord's way of being in the world for Sivavakkiyar and the devotee's for Pattiragiriyar.

The Naladiyar says the scheming of women whose minds are with another man is plainly known and fools still do not grasp it; Pattiragiriyar takes a woman whose mind is elsewhere even in her husband's pleasure as the model for keeping the Lord's feet in his thought. The straying wife is the ethical poem's warning and the Siddhar's figure for devotion; the moral domain and the devotional one use her oppositely.

Tirumular says that even one who makes his bones firewood and fries his flesh cannot reach the gem unless he melts with love (அன்போடு உருகி) and softens within; Pattiragiriyar asks when his body, love and bones will melt (ஆகம் உருக அன்பு உருக என்பு உருக) and the experience of enjoyment join him. Both set melting against burning as the way to the Lord, and Pattiragiriyar's bones melt where Tirumular's are burned to no purpose.

Tirumular: for all who see the holy dance, tears of grace drip, the heart melts and the nectar of bliss wells up in the light within; Pattiragiriyar asks for body, love and bone to melt and the experience of enjoyment to come, with tears like pearls in 61 and the honey of Siva-bliss in 66. The sequence melting, tears, nectar is the same in both.

The Naladiyar's body is a bubble in pelting rain, forming and bursting again and again, and those who see it so resolve to end their wandering; Pattiragiriyar's life is a bubble on water (நீரில் குமிழி) to be left so that the flood of grace may rise. The bubble leads to a resolve in the Naladiyar and to a request for grace in Pattiragiriyar.

Sivavakkiyar mocks those who beat the drum through the town that the body is as unstable as a bubble on water (நீரினில் குமிழி ஒத்த நிலையிலாத காயம்), promise jnana-siddhi and seize others' goods; Pattiragiriyar says the same words of his own life (நிலையற்ற வாழ்வை) and asks to leave it. Sivavakkiyar does not deny the bubble; he denies the preachers, and Pattiragiriyar's saying it to himself is what the preachers do not do.

Tirumular's Shakti moves in the square, rests in the hexagon (அறுகோணம்) and moves in the circle, and Sadasiva is her form; Pattiragiriyar's Mahesvara lives in the hexagon of air and his Sadasiva in the circular path (72). The same shapes house the gods in both, with the square, hexagon and circle in the same order; which centre each shape marks is not fixed in either.

Tirumular lists Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Mahesvara and the five-faced one above them, with bindu, nada and Shakti, and makes Sadasiva common to all; Pattiragiriyar's 68 to 72 climb the same five gods in the same order, each in a shape in the body, ending at Sadasiva in the circle. Tirumular gives the order as cosmology, Pattiragiriyar as a ladder of centres to be seen within.

Tirumular: taking up ida and pingala and twisting at the root in the triangle (முக்கோணிலும்), one may see the feet of the Lord who holds time; Pattiragiriyar asks to worship Rudra who appears in the triangle with its three rings. The triangle is a centre in the body in both, at the root in Tirumular and, by the order of the gods, higher in Pattiragiriyar.

source_issues: 60: எவ்வனத்தின் and கவ்வனத் are unusual forms, perhaps for எவ்வணத்தின் and கவ்வும்; the first line may be corrupt.
73: கிடை in உச்சிக் கிடை நடுவே is uncertain.
